messages:
Zoe: Hey team, ran nsys on the recent KV-cache perf regression and most CUDA kernels show up as <unknown> in the timeline. No line info. Anyone seen this?
Anya: Yep. Usually means debug symbols missing or CUPTI mismatch. Did you build the runtime with -g / keep debug info in the .so?
Zoe: We build with -O2 and strip in the Dockerfile for smaller images.
Matt: Stripping in the container will remove symbol tables. Check for any `strip` or `--strip-all` in the final stage. Distroless bases also often don't include debuginfo.
Kevin: Also check the shared objects inside the container: `readelf -S /opt/runtime/lib/*.so | grep debug` or `objdump --syms` to confirm.
Zoe: run these now.
perf-bot: nsys summary: 120ms total cuda time, 70% attributed to unknown kernels, 0 symbolized. Trace file: /tmp/nsys-runs/trace.qdrep
Anya: If you use nsys inside a container, CUPTI from the container must match the driver/host. Mismatched CUPTI causes the profiler to fail symbolization. Which CUDA toolkit is in the image?
Zoe: Image has cuda-toolkit 11.8, host driver is 525.x (seems compatible), but the build pipeline uses a different dev image with 12.x. Could that be it?
Matt: Yes. If the build and runtime toolkits differ, the binary's DWARF/relocations can mismatch. Ideally run profiling in an image that matches the one used to compile and that exposes CUPTI: `/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so` must be present.
Anya: Quick checklist I use: 
```
# 1) Build with debug symbols
export CFLAGS="-g -O2 -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
# for C++ ext / runtime
cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo ..
# 2) Don't strip final binary (remove any 'strip' step)
# 3) Ensure container has CUPTI / cuda-tools installed
# 4) Use same CUDA toolkit version for build/profile image
```
Kevin: Also for Python extension .so: pip wheel / manylinux builds often strip symbols. Add `--global-option=build_ext --debug` or set environment `CFLAGS` during wheel build.
Zoe: Good call. I see our Dockerfile has `RUN strip /usr/local/bin/runtime` in the final stage. Removing that should help.
Matt: For quick local debugging, run nsys from a non-distroless debug image: `docker run --gpus all -it --rm --ipc=host -v $(pwd):/work nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:11.8-devel-ubi8 /bin/bash` then install your runtime and run `nsys profile -o /work/trace --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt python -u serve.py`
Anya: If symbols still missing, use `nsys profile --sample=cpu` to get CPU-side stacks; for CUDA-specific you can also try `nvprof --profile-from-start off --output-profile timeline.nvprof` (nvprof deprecated but sometimes gives different symbol results).
Zoe: After removing the strip and rebuilding inside 11.8-devel image, I still see a few important kernels un-symbolized (mostly small memcpy-ish kernels from our KV cache path).
Kevin: Small kernels sometimes get inlined or optimized out. Build with `-fno-inline` for a test build to see if they appear. Also `-rdynamic` on the linker helps export symbols from the main binary.
Anya: Another gotcha: when using JITed CUDA (e.g., cuBLAS/cudnn kernels), symbolization will show vendor kernel names, not your source. For our custom kernels in the runtime, make sure they weren't compiled with `-s` or stripped by the packager.
Matt: FYI CUPTI version logs: `nsys status report` shows CUPTI path used. If it points to host CUPTI but the container lib is different, you'll get incomplete line info. Mounting host's `/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI` into the container at the same path is a pragmatic fix for CI profiling.
Zoe: Great. Will try: rebuild with debug flags, remove strip, match toolkit, mount CUPTI. Will post results.
Anya: If you still see missing symbols after that, upload the `.qdrep` to the perf bucket and I can open it in nsight on my laptop. Sometimes the timeline linker in the UI recovers names better than CLI.
Zoe: Quick follow-up: rebuilding with `-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG` and profiling in the devel image fixed ~90% of the unknowns. Remaining unknowns are vendor kernels and a few inlined helpers.
Kevin: Nice. For the vendor stuff, you can rely on function-level hotspots and annotate with NVTX around batching/KV code paths to map timeline regions to source logic.
Matt: Also consider adding a CI job: `profile-smoke` that builds debug image and runs a short nsys trace to ensure symbolization works across releases. Prevents regressions where packaging strips again.
Zoe: Adding that to the backlog. Thanks all :tada:
